assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a single microwave photon strongly coupled to a controllable artificial atom on a chip, opening a new regime of light-matter interaction and supplying the readout, coupling and control architecture that underlies superconducting quantum processors. It is a clean demonstration of quantum optics with engineered circuits, and the work has been reproduced and extended in many laboratories. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and cQED is the natural, distinct follow-on rather than a repeat.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and collaborators) are tightly linked. Schoelkopf and Wallraff carry the experimental realisation and Blais the theory; Girvin is a close fourth contributor and excluding him is a real credit question. I work in this area and know several of these people, so my judgement should be read with that in mind.
assessment.maturity: Strong-coupling observation dates from 2004 and has been confirmed repeatedly. Dispersive readout, circuit-QED gates and error-correction experiments rest on it. Recognition is timely, with no sign of premature interpretation.
uncertainties: Girvin's role versus Blais as the theory representative is a real allocation question.
Overlap with the 2025 prize in the public mind could lead others to judge the subfield already recognised.
I have a personal and programmatic closeness to this field and cannot claim full neutrality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how to compute with trapped ions, and experiments then demonstrated gates, entanglement and digital quantum simulation with very high fidelity. This is the best-controlled quantum hardware platform in the physical detail that matters. The scientific contribution is a concrete route from fundamental quantum control to computation and simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller for the 1995 proposal and later theory. Blatt for the leading realisations of ion-trap gates and algorithms. Others, such as Wineland (already a laureate in 2012) and Monroe, also contributed decisively, which complicates a three-person configuration. Dropping Monroe and Haeffner-type contributors is a judgement.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation by several groups. The ion control behind the 2012 prize overlaps, so the new recognised contribution has to be the computing and simulation proposal.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland and Haroche prize may weigh against it.
Credit to Monroe and others for the first gate implementations is not captured in the supplied names.
I am less expert on ion-trap details than on superconducting circuits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, with the Mott insulator transition as a landmark observation and quantum-gas microscopes giving single-site resolution. It turned a theorist's model Hamiltonian into a controllable laboratory system, opening a new regime for studying correlated matter. The physics is clear and has been reproduced widely.
assessment.attribution: Greiner (Mott insulator observation, Bloch group), Bloch (lattice quantum simulation and microscopy) and Esslinger (fermionic Hubbard physics) are the decisive experimentalists. Cirac and Zoller proposed the optical-lattice Hubbard idea, but they also appear under trapped ions, and the proposal of Jaksch is not in the supplied names. A three-person experimental configuration is defensible, though the theory credit is left out.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the experimental sense. Quantum-simulation payoff for open problems such as the doped Hubbard model is still developing, so the claim to solve hard problems is not yet established.
uncertainties: The theory credit (Jaksch, Zoller, Cirac) cannot be fully reflected within the supplied names.
Whether quantum simulation has yet answered an open question in condensed matter is still debated.
Overlap with the 2001 and 2005 cold-atom prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes and the threshold theorem showed that fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in principle. This is central to the whole field and a decisive conceptual advance. As someone whose programme depends on error correction, I regard it as foundational, though it is more theoretical than discovery physics.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane for the first quantum codes and Kitaev for fault-tolerant ideas and the toric code. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov and Ben-Or, Preskill and others made decisive contributions, so any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature, but the experimental demonstration of below-threshold logical qubits is recent and still ongoing. The Nobel standard of physical discovery rather than mathematical or computer-science insight is a concern.
uncertainties: Many co-founders (Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov) are not in the supplied names.
Whether it counts as physics discovery for the prize or as mathematical and computer-science work.
Experimental validation of scalable fault tolerance is still in progress.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposal of spin qubits in quantum dots (Loss-DiVincenzo) and the experimental control of single and two-qubit spin operations, now moving into silicon with promising CMOS compatibility. A clear route from fundamental spin physics to scalable qubits, with attention to the physical details of coherence and exchange.
assessment.attribution: Loss for the proposal, Tarucha and Vandersypen for realisation of spin control and readout. DiVincenzo's coauthorship of the proposal is not available in the supplied names. Others, such as Marcus, Petta and Morello, also made major experimental advances.
assessment.maturity: The key experiments are well confirmed across groups. Fault-tolerant-scale performance has not been shown, so it is more a platform than a closed discovery.
uncertainties: DiVincenzo and experimentalists such as Petta, Marcus and Morello are not in the credited set.
The competitive standing of spin qubits against other platforms is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics reached the quantum regime of mechanical motion, with ground-state cooling, squeezing and quantum-coherent coupling. It extends the macroscopic quantum control theme of the 2025 prize into a different physical platform and is close to my own area of microwave quantum optics with mechanical elements.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg and Painter led the optical and microwave-optical realisations of quantum control. Cleland, who demonstrated quantum ground-state and phonon control in a piezo resonator, also has a decisive claim, so a three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: The central results are confirmed by multiple groups. Applications such as transduction are still developing, though the discovery claim itself is well established.
uncertainties: Cleland's early quantum-ground-state demonstration makes the exclusion contentious.
Application payoff is not established.
Whether there is a single clear discovery as opposed to a set of related advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantized conductance in ballistic point contacts is a clean, visible experimental demonstration of quantum transport in a controllable nanostructure. It underpins mesoscopic physics and led to quantum-dot and nanoelectronic devices. It is also close to my own training in mesoscopic transport.
assessment.attribution: Two groups discovered it independently and simultaneously in 1988: van Wees and van Houten with colleagues at Delft and Philips, and Wharam, Pepper and colleagues at Cambridge. The supplied credit omits Wharam, and van Houten and van Wees share a result with Pepper, so the allocation among three is a genuine question.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed immediately, but its age and the long gap since the discovery raise the question of why now. Landauer's earlier theory and the 1985 quantum Hall prize cover adjacent ground.
uncertainties: Wharam and other Cambridge co-authors are not available in the supplied names.
The case for recognition so long after the 1988 discovery is not obvious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase established that gauge potentials and geometry have physical, observable consequences. This is an influential idea with lasting effects across condensed matter, optics and quantum control. In my own field the geometric phase appears in qubit gate design.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (Bohm is deceased and not in the supplied names) and Berry are the main figures. Only two names are available, which is a defensible but incomplete credit pairing. Pancharatnam and Ehrenberg-Siday also have priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades. The recognition is long overdue rather than premature, but it is also a foundational concept rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Bohm's central role in Aharonov-Bohm cannot be recognised by the prize because he is deceased.
Priority claims by Ehrenberg-Siday and Pancharatnam.
Whether the committee treats it as one discovery or two.
